gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-noto-sans-nko-unj: Bold and blunt, Comic Relief draws every stroke with the same pen pressure. Noto Sans NKo Unjoined is the friendlier voice, its small letters wide open and approachable beneath that heading.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-noto-sans-old-sou: Comic Relief has a tube-like stroke that looks like neon glass, bold and commanding in the heading spot. Noto Sans Old South Arabian is the plain sans that stays clean, its curves ending before they turn inward.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-noto-sans-shavian: Comic Relief keeps a steady, marker-like line weight, and its bowls are left unfinished on one side for a loose, commanding look. It earns its keep big and short, beside Noto Sans Shavian.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-ojuju: Approachable and contemporary, Ojuju has thins that never turn spindly, like a lightly flexed spring wire. Comic Relief is where the stitched-thread strokes get to be big and short, a loud headline partner.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-overpass: Overpass reads modern and professional, never letting bold-looking and light-looking strokes mix inside a single word. But Comic Relief does the loud, commanding heading work, while the plain sans handles the quieter detail.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-palanquin: Palanquin gives curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths, a professional, contemporary sans for the text. And Comic Relief, traced with a single thickness, is the bolder voice that commands attention up top.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-philosopher: Every curve in Comic Relief is as thick as a straight stem, which gives the heading a bold, blunt character. But Philosopher does the finer work, with soft shifts in thickness and plenty of daylight inside its curves.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-pontano-sans: Comic Relief hits hard with contrast-free strokes from stem to terminal. Make that heading small, though, and its commanding weight fades, while Pontano Sans with its wide open terminals is fine even at larger sizes.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-pt-sans: Approachable and professional, PT Sans forms its c as an open arc. Beneath it, Comic Relief's bent-tubing letters hold the same gauge throughout, so a longer passage would feel friendly rather than heavy.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-quattrocento-sans: Loud, loose and unmistakably bold, Comic Relief pushes up and side strokes to the same weight, while Quattrocento Sans keeps clear gaps so its c never looks like an o. One shouts, the other tidies up.
